nodes.description: Explain how the definition of the meaning of rational exponents follows from extending the properties of integer exponents to those values, allowing for a notation for radicals in terms of rational exponents. edges.reason: The actual criterion expressly asks how cube roots differ from square roots; square-root meaning is required for that comparison, although not for defining a cube root alone.
edges.scope: contrasting cube roots with square roots

edges.reason: The proposed strict rationale refers to arithmetic-square-root meaning, but that is node cnm_074. Node cnm_075 is specifically computation of perfect-square roots and sqrt(a squared), which the domain criterion need not use.
edges.scope: Root-calculation examples as background to radical notation

edges.reason: A quadratic radical denotes the principal square root. The condition that the radicand is nonnegative comes directly from negative numbers having no real square roots.
edges.scope: meaning of the radical symbol and nonnegative radicand

edges.reason: For the source's linear-radicand letter-range tasks, finding allowed values solves the radicand's nonnegativity inequality; the edge is limited to that case.
edges.scope: finding the letter range that makes the radical defined

edges.reason: The square-root identities are real-valued only on the stated nonnegative radicand domain; that condition must be interpreted.
edges.scope: conditions a≥0 attached to each property

edges.reason: Negative-power reciprocals are explicitly reused in the criteria.
The square-root-to-half-power rewrite needs even-root meaning and real-domain restrictions.
edges.scope: Rewriting radicals and their meaningful domain
